findings.title: Derived checkpoint treated as co-authoritative: kill/crash between ledger append and checkpoint rename permanently bricks an intact mission
findings.summary: Append_Current_Event durably fsyncs the ledger record before writing the checkpoint. A SIGKILL/crash (or checkpoint-write failure) in that window leaves the authoritative append-only ledger at sequence N+1 while checkpoint.ncp holds N. Load_Mission demands an exact ledger/checkpoint match and returns Store_Corrupt with no path to rebuild the derived checkpoint from the authoritative ledger, so a fully hash-chain-valid mission becomes permanently unloadable — violating the 'kill-during-commit leaves a consistent state' invariant.

evidence.label: commit ordering
evidence.explanation: Ledger append is fsynced and verified (223-231), then Save_Checkpoint runs (233); a kill between 232 and 234 durably advances the ledger but not the checkpoint.
evidence.excerpt: Recover(...);\n if Recovered.Status /= Recovered_Valid ... then Result:=Store_Corrupt ...\n Context.Ledger_Head:=...; Save_Checkpoint(Home,Context,Checkpoint_OK);

evidence.label: recovery rejects intact ledger
evidence.explanation: Load_Mission requires Recovered.Sequence = Checkpoint.Sequence (and state/head); any skew -> Store_Corrupt (454), with no rebuild-from-ledger path.
evidence.excerpt: if Recovered.Status /= Recovered_Valid or else Checkpoint_Status /= Checkpoint_Valid or else Recovered.Sequence /= Checkpoint.Sequence ... then Result := Store_Corrupt;

optionalProperties.precondition: Kill/crash or checkpoint-write failure after ledger fsync (mission_store.adb:232) and before checkpoint rename (mission_store.adb:233).
optionalProperties.remediation: On recovery accept checkpoint.sequence <= ledger head and rebuild the checkpoint from the authoritative ledger tail instead of failing to Store_Corrupt, or make the checkpoint pointer advance atomically with the ledger append.

findings.title: Missing containing-directory fsync (and macOS F_FULLFSYNC) after temp+rename / file create weakens power-loss durability
findings.summary: Object, checkpoint, reference, and ledger writers implement temp+rename / append+fsync but never fsync the containing directory after rename/create, and use plain fsync() which is not durable on macOS/APFS without F_FULLFSYNC. Under OS crash/power loss a just-committed rename or new ledger file can be lost, leaving a mission missing an object/reference/checkpoint/ledger and failing to load. The documented 'temp+rename+dir-sync' pattern is only partially implemented. Process-kill (the primary stated threat) is unaffected.

locations.role: file create/append fsync only, no dir sync; plain fsync

evidence.label: object store
evidence.explanation: Put fsyncs the temp file then Rename_File with no directory fsync.

evidence.label: plain fsync on macOS
evidence.explanation: fsync is imported as the C 'fsync', which on APFS does not flush to stable storage; F_FULLFSYNC is required for real durability on the stated macOS target.
evidence.excerpt: function Fsync (FD : Interfaces.C.int) return Interfaces.C.int with Import, Convention => C, External_Name => "fsync";

optionalProperties.precondition: OS crash / power loss (not a plain process kill), and/or macOS APFS fsync semantics.
optionalProperties.remediation: fsync the containing directory fd after each rename/create; on macOS use fcntl(fd,F_FULLFSYNC) for ledger/checkpoint/object/reference writes.
